subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should ordinary Gateway startup ever persist doctor repairs automatically, and if so which repair classes are safe enough for unattended startup execution?
rationale: Current source and docs deliberately validate-and-guide instead of mutating persistent config during startup, while the issue discussion shows both real drift pain and concrete safety regressions from a startup `doctor --fix` workaround.

options.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
options.body: Leave ordinary Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, fix narrower doctor bugs separately, and keep persistent config repair operator-initiated.

options.title: Add Opt-In Safe Startup Repair
options.body: Define an allowlisted repair subset with backups, changed-path logs, protected-value rules, and upgrade tests before exposing a named opt-in setting or service flag.

options.title: Auto-Apply By Default
options.body: Permit default startup self-healing only if maintainers explicitly accept the compatibility and security risk with broad release proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
recommendation.body: Leave ordinary Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, fix narrower doctor bugs separately, and keep persistent config repair operator-initiated.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest central history on doctor-owned config repair and the decision is primarily a product/security policy boundary for that repair surface.
